date_note: Intrusion confirmed Oct 6 and first announced Oct 9; the investigation report is dated Nov 16.
title: Enecom finishes probe of October breach: 2,940 personal records leaked or possibly leaked
summary: Enecom's investigation report of November 16 says an intruder used an improperly obtained maintenance account to enter its internal network through the thin-client environment, then used several employees' valid credentials. 2,940 personal records, 1,838 of them employees', were leaked or possibly leaked. Bank and card data were not included, and no misuse has been found.
plain: A Hiroshima telecom company says hackers used a stolen maintenance login to reach its internal network and may have taken contact details of 2,940 people.
exec: Shows how a single stolen vendor-style maintenance account opened a whole internal network.
action: Audit and expire maintenance and vendor accounts, restrict thin-client and remote-access paths, and enforce device-bound multi-factor authentication.

sources.name: Enecom (first notice via Security News Lab)

validation.note: Company's own report read in full, plus Chugoku Shimbun (partial, paywalled) for the 2,940 figure. Ransomware not mentioned in the notice.
